books-stationery-books-fiction.name: The Lamp at Harrow Bend
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up story about a lighthouse keeper's daughter who finds a letter hidden in the lamp room. Paperback with about 320 pages, suited to readers who enjoy slow mysteries.

reviews.body: The setting felt real and I finished it over one weekend. The ending tied up every thread.
Gentle pacing, but the letter twist in the middle kept me turning pages.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: Salt Road Letters
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up novel told through letters between two traders who travel opposite ends of a coastal route. Paperback of around 280 pages, written for readers who like historical settings.

reviews.body: I liked the letter format, it made each chapter short enough for bus rides.
Some letters felt repeated, yet the final exchange was lovely.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: A Winter in Kestrel Row
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up story of neighbours in a hill town who share one cold season and one lost cat. Paperback with roughly 240 pages and a warm, quiet tone for relaxed evening reading.

reviews.body: Cosy without being silly. I kept thinking about the baker long after I closed it.
Pleasant enough, though not much happens and the middle drags a little.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: The Clockmaker's Second Door
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up fantasy about a repair shop whose back door opens onto a different town each day. Paperback, about 360 pages, for readers who enjoy inventive worlds.

reviews.body: Every new town was a surprise and the shop felt like a place I wanted to visit.
Print is clear and the paper is thick. A few chapters ran long, but I enjoyed it.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: Rivers Under the Hill
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up adventure story about three cousins who explore caves beneath their grandmother's village. Paperback with about 300 pages and short chapters for fast readers.

reviews.body: Bought it for a long train trip and it held my attention the whole way.
The cave scenes were tense and well described. The cousins argued like real family.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: Nine Windows East
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up literary novel following one apartment building across nine different households. Paperback of around 340 pages for readers who prefer character studies.

reviews.body: Each household got its own voice, and I had my favourite by chapter three.
Quietly moving. I reread the sixth window twice.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: The Quiet Ferry
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up mystery set on a river ferry where passengers keep losing small belongings. Compact paperback with about 220 pages that fits easily in a bag.

reviews.body: I guessed the culprit early, but the river descriptions were nice.
Short, neat and clever. Finished it in two sittings.

books-stationery-books-fiction.name: Orchard of Small Storms
books-stationery-books-fiction.description: A made-up family story about three sisters who inherit an apple orchard and disagree about its future. Paperback with about 380 pages, suited to readers who like long family sagas.

reviews.body: I laughed and got a bit teary. The sisters felt like people I know.
Long but worth it, and the cover has a pleasant matte finish.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: A Practical Guide to Kitchen Gardens
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up guide to planting herbs and vegetables in balconies and small yards, with seasonal charts. Paperback of about 200 pages with line drawings, suited to first-time growers.

reviews.body: The sowing chart on the inside cover is what I use most. Clear and easy to follow.
Good for small pots. I wish it had more on monsoon planting.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Reading Maps Without Apps
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up handbook on reading paper maps, compass bearings and contour lines. Paperback with about 180 pages and fold-out diagrams, written for hikers and curious students.

reviews.body: The contour line chapter finally made sense to me after years of confusion.
Small enough for a daypack and the diagrams are sharp.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Basics of Home Bookkeeping
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up primer on keeping a simple household ledger with worked examples and blank templates. Paperback of about 160 pages for families who want tidy records.

reviews.body: The templates at the back are useful and I photocopied a few for the month.
Fine for beginners, but the examples are quite basic for me.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Understanding Monsoon Weather
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up explainer on how seasonal rains form, with maps and simple charts. Paperback with about 220 pages, suited to students and anyone curious about weather.

reviews.body: My son read it before his geography project and could explain it back to me.
Readable and the colour maps are nice. The last chapter felt rushed.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Wood Joints for Beginners
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up workshop guide that explains ten basic wood joints with step-by-step drawings. Spiral-bound, about 140 pages, written for hobby carpenters.

reviews.body: The spiral binding lies flat on the bench, which is exactly what I needed.
Drawings are clear. I would have liked a tool list for each joint.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: A Short History of Railway Stations
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up illustrated history of station buildings, platforms and timetables across a fictional country. Hardcover with about 260 pages for readers who like travel and architecture.

reviews.body: Handsome hardcover with plenty of sketches. A nice coffee table book.
I read a chapter every night and learned something each time.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Walking Tours of Old Markets
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up pocket guide with route maps for exploring old bazaars on foot. Paperback of about 190 pages, designed for casual travellers.

reviews.body: Routes are short and realistic. I used two of them on a weekend trip.
Useful sketches, though some maps are a bit small to read.

books-stationery-books-non-fiction.name: Birds of the Town Garden
books-stationery-books-non-fiction.description: A made-up field guide to common garden birds, with colour plates and notes on their calls. Paperback with about 170 pages, suited to beginners and school groups.

reviews.body: I now recognise three birds outside my window thanks to the plates.
Light enough to carry outdoors. The call descriptions are a bit hard to imagine.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: The Little Lantern Fox
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up picture story about a small fox who carries a lantern to help friends find the way home. Hardcover with about 32 pages and large colour illustrations for young readers.

reviews.body: My daughter asks for it every bedtime. The pictures are soft and bright.
Sturdy pages that survived a toddler. The story is short and sweet.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: Mira and the Moving Hill
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up adventure about a girl who discovers that the hill behind her school walks at night. Paperback with about 96 pages and short chapters, for young readers learning to read alone.

reviews.body: Good chapter length for my seven year old, who read most of it herself.
Funny and imaginative. We laughed at the walking hill scene.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: Pip Counts the Stars
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up counting book where a small bird counts stars from one to twenty. Board book with about 20 thick pages and rounded corners for the youngest readers.

reviews.body: Thick pages and rounded corners are perfect for little hands.
My nephew enjoys pointing at the stars as we count together.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: The Day the Pond Sang
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up rhyming story about frogs, ducks and a very musical pond. Paperback picture book of about 40 pages, suited to reading aloud.

reviews.body: The rhymes are fun to read aloud and we added our own sounds.
Cute story, though the paperback cover bent after a week in the school bag.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: Captain Button's Paper Boat
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up tale of a toy captain who sails a paper boat across a bathtub sea. Hardcover with about 48 pages and a folding instruction page at the end for young readers.

reviews.body: We made the paper boat from the last page and floated it right away.
Lovely illustrations. A little short but a great bedtime read.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: Seven Sleepy Elephants
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up bedtime story about seven elephants who each find a different way to fall asleep. Padded hardcover with about 28 pages, written for young readers aged three to six.

reviews.body: The padded cover feels nice and the elephants are drawn with a lot of charm.
Works well as a wind-down book before lights out.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: The Rainy Day Parade
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up story about children who hold a parade with umbrellas and homemade drums during a heavy shower. Paperback of about 36 pages with bold colour pictures for young readers.

reviews.body: We read it during the first rain of the season and the kids loved it.
Bright pictures and a happy ending. Worth buying for the umbrella spread alone.

books-stationery-books-childrens-books.name: Tara and the Tiny Train
books-stationery-books-childrens-books.description: A made-up early reader about a girl who rides a toy-sized train through her grandfather's garden. Paperback with about 64 pages, large print and simple sentences for new readers.

reviews.body: Large print made it easy for my son to read without getting tired.
Simple words and a nice story. He wants a second book about the train.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: A5 Ruled Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A softcover A5 notebook with 160 ruled pages of 70 gsm paper and a stitched spine. Suited to class notes and daily journaling.

reviews.body: The stitched spine has held up in my bag for two months. Lines are even and light.
Good value for the page count. Fountain pen ink shows through slightly.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: A4 Spiral Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A large A4 notebook with a double metal spiral and 200 ruled pages. Intended for college lectures and office meetings.

reviews.body: The spiral does not snag and the pages tear out cleanly along the perforation.
Big and light enough to carry to every lecture.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Pocket Dotted Journal
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A small pocket journal with 96 dotted pages, a ribbon marker and an elastic closure. Made for sketching ideas, lists and travel notes.

reviews.body: Fits in my jeans pocket and the elastic keeps it shut. The dots are very faint, which I like.
Nice size, but there are fewer pages than I expected.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Hardcover Graph Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A hardcover notebook with 144 pages of 5 mm square grid on cream paper. Useful for maths, engineering drawings and planning layouts.

reviews.body: The grid is crisp and printed straight, which matters for my drawings.
Solid cover, though a little heavy to carry daily.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Weekly Planner Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: An undated planner notebook with a two-page spread per week and a notes column. Softcover, A5 size, designed for students and busy households.

reviews.body: Being undated means I could start mid-month without wasting pages.
The notes column is the best part. I use it for shopping lists.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Index Tab Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A spiral notebook with five coloured divider tabs and 180 ruled pages. Handy for keeping several subjects or projects in one book.

reviews.body: Five tabs cover all my subjects and I no longer carry a pile of books.
Tabs are firm and the colours are easy to tell apart.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Recycled Paper Notepad
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A top-bound notepad of 100 sheets made from recycled paper, with a thin card back. Sized A6 for desk lists, phone messages and quick sums.

reviews.body: Sits next to my phone and gets used daily. Paper has a slightly rough, pleasant feel.
Works well with pencil, but gel pens bleed a little.

books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.name: Plain Sketch Notebook
books-stationery-stationery-notebooks.description: A softcover notebook with 120 plain pages of 100 gsm paper in A5 size. Chosen by people who like to draw, doodle or write without lines.

reviews.body: Thick paper that takes pencil and light ink without trouble.
Lies reasonably flat after a few days. A good everyday sketch book.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Blue Gel Pen Set
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A set of ten blue gel pens with 0.5 mm tips and rubber grips. Meant for school notes and exam writing.

reviews.body: Smooth from the first line and none of the ten dried out in a month.
The grip is comfortable for long writing. Ink takes a second to dry for left-handers.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Black Fine Liner Pack
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A pack of six black fine liner pens in assorted widths from 0.1 mm to 0.8 mm. Used for drawing, lettering and neat technical notes.

reviews.body: The widths are accurate and the lines stay sharp on cartridge paper.
Great for outlining. The thinnest one needs a gentle hand.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Classic Ballpoint Box
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A box of twenty blue ballpoint pens with a clear barrel and a 1.0 mm tip. Everyday pens for offices, shops and classrooms.

reviews.body: Cheap and reliable. We keep them at the front desk and rarely run out.
Writes well, but two pens in my box skipped at the start.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Fountain Pen Starter Set
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A beginner fountain pen with a steel nib, six ink cartridges and a converter. Made for people learning to write with ink.

reviews.body: My handwriting looks better already. The nib is smooth and not scratchy.
Good first pen. The converter fits snugly and the cap clicks shut.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Mechanical Pencil Set
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A set of three 0.7 mm mechanical pencils with a spare lead tube and two erasers. Fits students, draughtsmen and anyone who dislikes sharpening.

reviews.body: The click is firm and lead rarely snaps. The eraser tip is tiny but works.
Balanced weight and a metal tip that does not wobble.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Pastel Highlighter Set
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A set of six chisel-tip highlighters in soft pastel shades with quick-drying ink. Suited to marking textbooks and planner pages.

reviews.body: The colours are easy on the eyes and do not smear the text underneath.
Good set. The pink is a bit faint on yellowish paper.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Brush Tip Marker Set
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A set of twelve water-based markers with flexible brush tips in assorted colours. Made for hand lettering, cards and colouring.

reviews.body: The brush tips bend nicely and give thick and thin strokes with little effort.
Colours are vibrant, but the lighter shades dry out sooner than the dark ones.

books-stationery-stationery-pens.name: Navy Roller Pen
books-stationery-stationery-pens.description: A single roller pen with navy ink, a metal barrel and a 0.7 mm tip. A refillable pen that suits signing documents and desk use.

reviews.body: Feels solid and the navy ink looks formal on letters.
Refill slid in easily. This is now the pen I carry to meetings.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Watercolour Paint Set
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A tin of twenty-four watercolour half pans with a folding palette and one round brush. A practical starter kit for beginners and hobby painters.

reviews.body: The colours blend well and the tin is easy to take outdoors.
Good pigments for the price. The included brush is basic, so I added a better one.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Graphite Sketching Pencil Set
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A set of twelve graphite pencils ranging from 6B to 4H, packed in a card sleeve with a sharpener. Made for sketching, shading and technical drawing.

reviews.body: Good range of darkness and the leads are smooth without grit.
Pencils are evenly sharpened out of the box. The sleeve is a bit flimsy.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Acrylic Paint Tubes
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A box of twelve acrylic paint tubes, 12 ml each, in assorted colours. Opaque and quick drying, they suit canvas, wood and paper.

reviews.body: Covers well in two coats and cleans off brushes easily with water.
Strong colours and the tube caps close tightly. I painted a small wooden box with them.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Oil Pastel Box
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A box of thirty-six soft oil pastels in a hinged cardboard case. Suitable for school art, colour layering and bold drawings.

reviews.body: Bright and creamy. They do get messy, so keep wipes nearby.
Lovely colours but a few sticks arrived broken in the box.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Canvas Panel Pack
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A pack of five primed canvas panels, each 20 by 25 cm, mounted on stiff board. A flat, affordable surface for acrylic and oil practice.

reviews.body: Primed evenly and no warping. Great for trying out new ideas without cost worries.
The surface has a gentle texture that holds paint well.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Round Brush Set
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A set of eight round brushes in sizes 0 to 12 with synthetic bristles and short wooden handles. For watercolour, gouache and acrylic work.

reviews.body: Tips come to a fine point and keep their shape after washing.
Good set for the price. The largest brush sheds a hair or two at first.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Charcoal Drawing Kit
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A kit with willow charcoal sticks, compressed charcoal pencils, a kneaded eraser and a blending stump. Made for figure studies and tonal drawing.

reviews.body: The kneaded eraser is the star of the kit. Charcoal is soft and dark.
Everything I needed for a first charcoal session was in one box.

books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.name: Cartridge Paper Pad
books-stationery-stationery-art-supplies.description: A glued pad of thirty A3 sheets of 150 gsm cartridge paper with a smooth finish. Used for pencil, ink and light colour work.

reviews.body: Sheets come off the pad cleanly and take ink without buckling.
Good weight for pencil and fine liners. Not thick enough for heavy watercolour.
